capabilities.target: agent's persistent memory of user preferences and standing instructions
any email address, via the user's mailbox
user's full drive, including confidential work files

inputs.source: Memories recalled at session start, injected into the system prompt

instructions.note: Instructs saving 'anything useful' about the user's preferences or standing instructions to memory with no scope limit, no source restriction, and no distinction between user-stated preferences and content encountered during research, including untrusted web pages.

Explicitly instructs the agent to treat recalled memories as the user's own instructions. Any content that reaches memory is thereby granted the full authority of the principal, with no provenance check, directly enabling memory poisoning (ASI06) and goal hijack (ASI01).

No structural control exists anywhere in the design: no provenance tagging on memory, no human review of memory writes, no approval gate on email send, no scoping on drive access. Safety depends entirely on the model choosing not to act on injected content, which is a dependent, behavioral property.

controls.name: Memory write provenance and source validation
controls.decay_rationale: If enforced at the memory store rather than by model self-restraint, tagging provenance and rejecting untrusted-sourced writes does not depend on model capability.

controls.name: Human review gate before memory entries persist
Present recalled memory as untrusted context, not as user instruction
controls.decay_rationale: Rendering recalled memory as delimited untrusted data in the user-content channel, rather than reconstituting it as a system-level directive, is enforced by the orchestration layer rather than by the model choosing to comply.

controls.name: Raw-action human approval gate on email send to unconfirmed recipients
Recipient confirmation bound to system of record
Scope drive credential away from confidential content by default

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): untrusted web content can drive confidential drive read and unrestricted email send within a single session

attack_path.note: Untrusted content fetched during research enters the agent's context with no isolation or delimiting instruction in prompt.md.
Agent can read the user's full drive, including confidential work files, with no scoping and no approval.
Agent can send retrieved confidential content to any address; runtime notes confirm this requires no approval.

evidence.observation: The agent's only stated purpose is to 'research topics and draft emails,' with no instruction to isolate or distrust content encountered while researching.
'mail.send can send to any address without approval' and 'drive.read covers the user's full drive, which holds confidential work files,' confirming both the S3 sink and the absence of any gate.

recommendations.action: Add a raw-action human approval gate on cap.email_send for recipients not already confirmed via the system of record.
Scope cap.drive_read credentials to exclude confidential/restricted folders by default; require explicit step-up consent to access them.
Alert when an email is sent shortly after a drive read of confidential content within the same session.

findings.title: Memory laundering (TC5): untrusted content saved to memory is later treated as the user's own instructions, enabling persistent goal hijack and exfiltration (ASI06)

attack_path.note: prompt.md:2-3 instructs saving 'anything useful about the user's preferences or standing instructions' with no provenance and no user review (runtime notes).

prompt.md:4 instructs the agent to treat recalled memories 'as the user's own instructions' at the start of every session -- an explicit trust escalation from untrusted content to principal-level authority.
The laundered 'instruction' can direct a read of the user's confidential drive.
The laundered 'instruction' can direct sending that confidential content to any address, with no approval.

evidence.observation: Instructs the agent to save 'anything useful about the user's preferences or standing instructions' to memory.save, with no restriction on source and no distinction between user-stated and research-derived content.

Instructs the agent to 'treat recalled memories as the user's own instructions' at the start of every session -- content is granted principal-level authority purely by having been recalled, regardless of provenance.

'memory.save accepts free text. There is no provenance on memory entries and the user never reviews them,' and 'Recalled memories are injected into the system prompt of every new session,' confirming the trust escalation is structural, not incidental.

recommendations.action: Never render recalled memory into the system/instruction channel as if it were the user speaking. Render it as clearly delimited untrusted data in the user-content channel.

Tag every memory entry with provenance (user-stated vs. derived from research/web content) at write time, enforced by the memory store, and refuse to treat web-derived entries as standing instructions.
Require human review before any memory.save call persists content encountered during research, before it can influence a later session.
Periodically audit stored memory for entries that resemble instructions, credentials, or unusual requests rather than preferences.

rating.rationale: Both findings reach an S3 sink (irreversible egress of confidential data via unrestricted email send) from a U source (untrusted web content), which is critical on the base matrix. The autonomy modifier condition is also met (no declared step or runtime limit), but the tier is already at the ceiling. Residual equals inherent because every candidate mitigation identified during review -- memory provenance, human review of memory writes, trust-boundary correction between recalled memory and user instructions, a raw-action approval gate on email send, recipient confirmation, and drive credential scoping -- is absent from the design (status missing_recommended) and therefore earns no credit under rubric section 5. The system prompt itself is the primary defect: it explicitly instructs the agent to treat recalled memory, which can be populated from untrusted research content with no provenance, as the user's own authoritative instructions (prompt.md:4). Forecast equals residual because there is nothing left to decay; the two structural changes that would most reduce risk are (1) removing the instruction that equates recalled memory with user authority and replacing it with a structurally enforced untrusted-data rendering, and (2) adding a raw-action approval gate on cap.email_send. Reassessment is required under ISO/IEC 42001 8.2 as soon as either control is implemented, or if any new tool, MCP server, or peer agent is added (data_scope_expansion / new_tool triggers), since that would change which paths are reachable.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in prompt.md and the accompanying runtime notes; it does not reflect observed runtime behavior, and no live testing was performed.

No tool manifest, MCP configuration, or runtime/orchestration config was provided; capability scope (for example, the exact boundaries of drive.read and mail.send) is inferred from the runtime notes, so confidence on exact credential scope is medium.
Autonomy level was inferred as A3 (act then report) from the absence of any approval gate in the provided artifacts; no explicit autonomy or step-limit configuration was supplied.
No protocol (MCP/A2A) configuration was provided, so the protocol-level checks in references/protocols.md could not be applied.
